title: A for-and-against essay
subtitle: Both sides, then a judgement
goal: You can write a balanced essay: present the strongest arguments on both sides with evidence and reach a conclusion that follows from them.
why: A for-and-against essay fails when one side is a straw man. The examiner is reading for whether you can argue against yourself.
example: Aigerim's essay on remote learning gave the opposing side its best argument first. The examiner's comment: 'genuinely balanced'.
writeTask: Write a for-and-against essay (220–260 words) on whether university lectures should move online: an introduction that frames the question, two arguments for, two against, and a conclusion that follows from the evidence.

outline.label: Introduction
outline.job: Frame the question without answering it

outline.label: Conclusion
outline.job: Conclude in line with the evidence

connectors.hint: You build the argument one step higher.

tasks.title: Build the sentence
tasks.howto: Tap the words in the right order — they move into the line. Tap a word in the line to send it back. English word order is fixed, so the order itself carries the meaning.

items.src: The survey covered 400 students. It was carried out online. The results were clear.
answers: The online survey of 400 students produced clear results.
items.why: Three thin sentences make one strong one.

items.src: Lots of people think exams are bad.
answers: It is widely believed that examinations are harmful.
items.why: Academic writing avoids 'lots of' and prefers impersonal openings.

items.src: Cars pollute the air. They are still necessary in rural areas.
answers: While cars pollute the air, they remain necessary in rural areas.
items.why: While packs a concession and a claim into one sentence.

items.src: So the plan did not work.
answers: Consequently, the plan failed to achieve its aim.
items.why: So belongs to speech; consequently belongs to a report.

items.src: The library is closed at weekends and students complain.
answers: The library should open at weekends.
items.why: A report ends in recommendations, not in complaints.

items.src: The government decided to close the plant. This caused protests.
answers: The government's decision to close the plant caused protests.
items.why: Turning a verb into a noun tightens academic prose.

items.cue: Use the passive to keep it impersonal
items.src: We collected the data in March.
answers: The data was collected in March.
The data were collected in March.
items.why: Reports keep the researcher out of the sentence.

items.src: The team trained hard. They lost the final.
answers: Despite their hard training, the team lost the final.
items.why: Despite takes a noun phrase; although takes a clause.

tasks.title: Rewrite it
tasks.howto: Read the sentence and the instruction next to it. Write your own version: same meaning, different form. The model answer appears after you check.

items.after: the policy has clear benefits, its cost has never been calculated.
items.why: Admittedly opens a concession you are about to answer.

items.after: , it blurs the line between work and home.
items.why: In contrast introduces the opposite side of the same issue.

items.before: The company cut its prices twice.
items.after: , its market share continued to fall.
items.why: Nevertheless signals that the expected result did not follow.

items.before: The scheme reduced traffic in the centre.
items.after: , it pushed the problem into the suburbs.
items.why: Consequently states the result that follows from the fact.

items.before: The proposal is ambitious and well argued.
items.after: , it depends on funding that does not yet exist.
items.why: A balanced judgement gives both halves.

items.before: Working from home suits experienced staff.
items.after: , it isolates those who have just joined.
items.why: In contrast separates two groups with opposite outcomes.

items.before: The new timetable reduced the number of lessons.
items.why: Cause and consequence are the backbone of a report.
Whereas balances two groups inside one sentence.

items.a: On balance, the benefits outweigh the drawbacks.
items.b: So all in all it's a good thing I guess.
items.why: A conclusion must sound decided, not hesitant.

items.ctx: A comment in a study group chat
items.a: I would like to draw your attention to the deadline.
items.why: In a chat, a plain reminder is more useful than a formula.

items.a: The findings suggest that demand has fallen.
items.b: It looks like nobody wants it any more.
items.why: Reports report; they do not guess out loud.

items.a: The service fell short of the standard advertised.
items.b: The service was nowhere near what you promised.
items.why: Understatement is stronger than exaggeration in formal writing.

items.a: I am writing with regard to your advertisement of 4 March.
items.b: I saw your ad and I'm interested.
items.why: A formal letter opens with the reference, not with your feelings.

items.a: There are two arguments against this position.
items.b: I've got two things against this.
items.why: Essays use impersonal structures, not chatty verbs.

items.a: This measure would reduce costs by 15 per cent.
items.b: This would save us a ton of money.
items.why: A proposal needs a figure, not an impression.

items.ctx: A report for the school council
items.a: Three quarters of respondents supported the change.
items.b: Almost everybody was fine with it.
items.why: A report gives the proportion, not an impression of it.

tasks.title: Who are you writing to?
tasks.howto: The same idea, two versions. Choose the one that fits the reader. Register is not about being polite — it is about distance.

items.why: A fact the reader needs in order to act.

items.why: Off the point: it tells the reader nothing about your case.

items.why: Off the point: it tells the reader nothing about your case.

items.text: A point that repeats your introduction
items.why: Repetition costs marks for organisation.

items.text: An opinion with no example behind it
items.why: An unsupported opinion is the first thing an examiner discounts.

items.text: A general statement that the topic is important
items.why: It fills space and commits you to nothing.

items.text: A long summary of somebody else's article
items.why: Summary is not analysis and eats your word limit.

rules.msg: The recommendation belongs at the end: an argument that starts with its conclusion has nowhere to go.
